newsitem.title: UK: Australia, Argentina may compete more in wheat - IGC.
newsitem.headline: Australia, Argentina may compete more in wheat - IGC.

text.p: Major wheat exporters Australia and Argentina may enjoy increased competitiveness on world markets after their 1996 crops come in from December, the International Grains Council (IGC) said.
Farmers in both countries responded well to soaring wheat prices earlier this year and sharply increased planted area.

In its latest monthly report on Friday, the IGC estimated Australian wheat output in 1996 at 17.5 million tonnes, up from 16.6 million last year. Argentina's crop was put at 14.5 million tonnes compared with some 8.7 million in 1995.
Both Austalia and Argentina have traditional export markets, but a projected decline in demand from neighbouring countries could shift some of their excess supply to the world market, the IGC said.
This would increase competition with other top exporters such as the European Union (EU), Canada and the United States, it said.
"Lower demand in some of their traditional outlets may result in vigorous competition with Northern Hemisphere exporters in alternative markets," the IGC said.
China is a major buyer of Australian wheat but a better harvest picture this year is likely to reduce its import needs.
Argentina's main export market is Brazil, whose wheat crop is forecast to rise one million tonnes this year to 2.5 million.
Argentina and Australia account for 20 percent of world wheat trade.
